items.heading: A Career Change At 30
items.text: A career change at 30 in India rarely arrives as a single dramatic moment. It usually builds up the way most mid-career discomfort does: a role that no longer matches what you actually studied for, interests that have quietly drifted away from what the job demands, a pay band that has stopped moving while newer joiners close the gap, or skills that were once your edge starting to feel dated.

items.heading: Before You Pick a Direction
items.text: Before you pick a direction or spend money on a course, certification, or business idea, run your situation through The four questions , your fit, your situation, the job market and AI-proofing, adapted here for exactly what changes for you at 30 in India.

items.heading: Most Career
items.text: Most career-change advice online is written for someone with no dependents, no EMI, and a decade to recover from a wrong turn. That advice is not wrong, it is just not written for you. Comparing the two situations side by side is the fastest way to see exactly what needs to change in your plan.

visuals.heading: Why a Career Change At 30 India

columns: What it means for your decision
rows: 57% of Indian professionals would consider career pivoting, per LinkedIn's Career Pathways India survey of over 5,000 professionals
You are part of a majority sentiment, not an outlier making an unusual choice.
51% of professionals cite pay and designation impact as the reason they hold back from switching
Money is the honest blocker for most people, which is exactly why the EMI and runway math below deserves real attention, not vague optimism.
23% of employees aged 30-34 are actively seeking a career change, one of the higher rates across age bands
This is a normal stage-of-career pattern, not a sign that something has gone wrong specifically for you.
Among 30-34 year olds, 32% have shifted careers once and 21% twice, while 32% have made no career move at all
Not moving is also common, the goal here is a deliberate decision either way, not decision paralysis.

items.heading: Try Three Unrelated Fields Over
items.text: Try three unrelated fields over a few years without a real financial penalty.

items.heading: Take an Unpaid Internship
items.text: Take an unpaid internship or a low-paying entry role purely to learn.

items.heading: Move Cities or Take
items.text: Move cities or take a pay cut with minimal pushback from family, since expectations are still forming.

items.heading: Treat a "Wrong" First Job
items.text: Treat a "wrong" first job as normal, not as a story they have to explain to anyone.
